how_checked: Read all of sdk/ios/Sources (OuoSDK, OuoReplay, OuoReplayCore, OuoCrash, OuoCrashCore, OuoVitals) and the spec sections 0-15. Ran sdk/ios/test.sh (Command Line Tools, Swift Testing) bounded by perl alarm 900: 233 tests in 31 suites across 4 test targets, all passed (OuoSDKTests 77, OuoReplayCoreTests 98, OuoVitalsTests 34, OuoCrashTests 24). No simulator, no device, no wire capture against a fake collector; wire claims come from the OTLP encoder and its unit tests (EncodingTests LogsJSON/TracesJSON).

requirements.note: Meta rule on how SDKs are judged; nothing for the SDK to implement.

Logs and spans go as OTLP/HTTP JSON to /v1/logs and /v1/traces, but replay chunks are a custom gzip JSON document (kind=frames, schema 2) POSTed to /v1/replay/chunks on a separate replay endpoint (default port 4319), not OTLP.

Own event names are unprefixed (navigation, ui.tap, app.lifecycle, log, feedback, http.request, http.request.failed) and log lines carry an unprefixed `message` attribute; app custom attributes pass unfiltered.

architecture_notes: The iOS SDK is fully custom: ADR-0016 rejected opentelemetry-swift, so there is no OTel API/SDK, no TracerProvider or LoggerProvider, and the spec's section 1 plan (wrap opentelemetry-swift) is not followed. OuoSDK builds log records and spans itself and encodes them as OTLP/HTTP JSON (not protobuf), gzip, Basic auth, to /v1/logs and /v1/traces, with scope `ouo11y-ios` and no schema_url. Records are batched in memory for 1 s (64 per batch, 2048 pending) and then written to a DiskQueue outbox folder (5 MB / 500 requests, oldest dropped, no TTL), sent one request at a time with 1 s doubling to 30 s retries, no jitter, partial_success not read. Sessions are a synchronous state machine persisted in session.json with UUID ids, inactivity, 30 s background and 4 h max timeouts, a rotation on every cold start, and a per-install device.id on the resource; sampling uses an FNV/fmix hash shared with the RN SDK and drops everything in unsampled sessions, with no bypass set. Crashes (async-signal-safe C handlers plus NSException, chained), hangs (display link watchdog) and watchdog/OOM terminations are reported as `exception` records with ouo.exception.kind rather than app.crash/ouo.app.hang; vitals use ouo.app.start, ouo.screen.display and the spec-named app.jank. Replay is a separate pipeline: masked, JPEG frames with patches and touches, spooled and queued on disk, posted as custom gzip JSON (`frames` schema 2) to the collector's /v1/replay/chunks receiver, so it is not OTLP and has none of the spec's replay/stream/segment identity, sha256, end record or buffer mode. The largest structural gaps: non-OTLP replay, event naming that predates the spec (event.name kept, unprefixed custom names, no view id), no consent, beforeSend, URL sanitising, shutdown or drop reporting, no bypass sampling, and main-thread file I/O in start and session updates.
